newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat falls sharply late on Egypt rumor.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat falls sharply late on Egypt rumor.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures fell sharply in late dealings on a rumor Egypt had rejected a cargoe of U.S. wheat, traders said.
"There was a rumor Egypt cancelled a shipment of wheat," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Wheat broke to the day's lows in late dealings led by broad-based selling in the nearby December contract which lent credence to the Egyptian rumor, they said.
At least six commission houses sold between one-half million to one million bushels in late dealings, a trader said.

Bear spreading, a switch from the recent pattern of bull spreading, also was noted, traders said. Continental Grain did 200,000 March/December, Tenco Inc nearly one million March/December and R.J. O'Brien did a half million March/December, they said.
Wheat had struggled through the morning and had found support from early gains in corn and soybeans. But the corn/soy influence also evaporated which exacerbated the slide in wheat, they said.
Wheat closed two to 11-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 11-1/4 at $4.22-1/2.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, up from 15,531 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Prudential Securities bought 200 December $6.00 calls at 1/8 cent, bought 100 December $5.70 calls at 1/8 cent and bought 100 December $5.80 calls at 1/8 cent, the traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,500 contracts, down from 5,300 Tuesday.
